Default macOS pipelined engine reports supportsLogits=false — @Generable throws unsupportedCapability at generation time
Segmentation re-encodes unchanged images and lazy diffusion reloads components; malformed detector shapes look like a valid empty scene
The structure-to-compute mapping is apple/coreai-models loader policy, not a Core AI framework routing contract
Diffusion filename fallback can select a stale component when old and new exports coexist; ship an explicit schema-0.2 assets map
A failed structure summary silently defaults to dynamic GPU specialization options before the loaded functions reveal the real structure
Substring tensor-role discovery picks the first ambiguous match and can wire the wrong intermediate without a missing-name error
ImageSegmenter re-runs image_encode for every prompt; same-image feature reuse requires an application-owned intermediate cache
Detector postprocessing returns an empty array for malformed output ranks and lengths, indistinguishable from a valid no-object scene
Lazy diffusion unloading saves residency but repeated requests reload every component and repay stage-load latency
Core AI code paths vanish from Simulator builds — the 27.0 simulator SDK ships no CoreAI framework; device SDKs do

Scope note: signatures rest on doc prose and shipped repos, not Apple sample code — verify before relying
Adding .aimodel files without the Metal Toolchain fails the build with a Metal-compiler error that never names Core AI
Summary with includingStatistics:true is considerably slower on large models — pass false for structure probes
AOT compilation does not remove on-device specialization; specialize() controls when it runs, not how much work it does
Probing the cache with .default then loading with .gpu options misses the cache: the key includes SpecializationOptions
Delete-while-referenced: reference pages say an error is thrown, the article says deletion is silently deferred
Python load_function raises KeyError for a missing name; Swift returns nil — ported parity tests change shape
CoreAISegmentationEngine re-runs image_encode on every segment() call — the 76% speedup needs caller-side feature caching
Each concurrent run() allocates its own intermediate buffers on demand — parallelism silently multiplies scratch memory
Every in-flight run() gets its own auto-allocated intermediate buffers — scratch memory grows with no API to bound it
Community swift-lm hand-rolls an async mutex for run serialization — single-author alpha code, not Apple guidance
Xcode's model viewer shows ? for a dynamic dimension; NDArrayDescriptor.shape reports -1 — same fact, two spellings
preferredStrides/minimumByteCount on an unresolved dynamic descriptor is a programming error — resolve dimensions first
Community input validator: check unexpected/missing inputs, scalarType, rank, and per-axis -1-or-equal before run()
shape/strides come back as Span<Int>: no map/reduce/for-in — the obvious element-count reduce does not compile
Span is non-escapable and not a Sequence — shape.reduce(1,*) does not compile; write your own product helper
NDArray.RawView init(metalBuffer:) is explicitly unsafe aliasing and absent on watchOS — you own the synchronization
Indexing by hand while ignoring interleaveLayout reads the wrong elements — the strides are block strides for that axis
Assuming the output dtype from the input descriptor misreads bytes — outputs can be a different scalar type
Output scalarType can differ from the input's — inspecting the array itself is the only safe way to decode it
Float16 doesn't exist on Intel macOS — Apple's own code fatalErrors, so fp16 models crash x86_64 builds outright
Docs cite layout.scalarCount, which is not public API — an internal-doc leak; compute the element count yourself
InferenceValue.ndArray is a consuming read dressed as a getter — a nil-check consumes the value
The ndArray property consumes the InferenceValue on first access despite reading like a plain getter
if value.ndArray != nil consumes the value — the later real read then yields nothing
Outputs you pre-allocate views for are updated in place and omitted from the returned Outputs — lookups come back nil
An output with a provided view is updated in place and not included in returned Outputs — reading it there finds nothing
run() requires a mutable view for every state — omitting any state is an error; drive allocation from stateNames
&stateArrays[name]! per iteration force-unwraps under exclusivity checking — use stored properties or a ~Copyable box
The layout-conversion copy: a default-allocated tensor gets converted on every inference with no observable symptom
Contiguous row-major NDArray vs specialized layout: the framework copies your tensor every inference, forever, silently
Community state allocation: MTLBuffer sized by minimumByteCount with .storageModeShared, then memset to zero
Pre-allocating an output view forces a copy for constant-backed outputs the framework would otherwise return zero-copy
AsyncValue and its NDArray/pixel-buffer inits are unavailable on watchOS — the async pipeline API is not universal
ComputeStream(commandQueue:) is absent on watchOS; encoded inferences on one stream serialize by read/write dependencies
AsyncValue.ndArray returns a copy when the value wraps an MTLBuffer — the zero-copy path silently isn't
Reading .ndArray from an MTLBuffer-backed AsyncValue copies the data to avoid aliasing — use the MTLBuffer directly
Apple's two image-preprocessing files disagree: premultipliedLast vs noneSkipLast alpha, and one resize is square-only
EXIF orientation is handled by no layer — the same JPEG tensorizes differently depending on the loader
apple/coreai-models has zero EXIF handling and its two image entry points disagree — rotated photos give wrong tensors
Segment.box origin flips per platform — Apple's decoder flips Y on macOS; assuming one convention misplaces every box
A failed AOT load surfaces as 'CoreAIDelegates.AIModelError error 3', re-mapped downstream — the raw code names no cause
catch let error as AssetError placed after a bare catch compiles but never runs — keep the bare catch last
Community swift-lm defines rich typed asset errors (shape/dtype/state mismatches) the Apple runtime does not give you
Cheat sheet: InferenceValue.ndArray is a consuming read — access it once
NamedMutableViews.take is single-shot — a second take of the same name is fatal
NDArray(descriptor:) may allocate a non-contiguous, hardware-preferred layout — do not assume row-major bytes
shape/strides are Span<Int>, which is not a Sequence — no reduce/map/for-in
Write through mutatingSlice(at:) — other slice accessors do not write back to the array
view(as:) is consuming — taking a typed view ends the tensor's other uses
view<T>(as:) on a mutable array returns a MUTABLE view — writes go through even where you expected a read
minimumByteCount is a programming error while hasDynamicShape — resolve dimensions first
preferredStrides likewise traps on an unresolved dynamic descriptor
SpecializationOptions is part of the cache key — every distinct value mints a new multi-GB cache entry
AssetError covers ASSET operations only — inference and cache failures throw other, mostly untyped errors
metadata.platforms omissions are a docs bug; doc watchOS-unavailable notes contradict the captured SDK interface
Core AI has zero Apple sample-code projects (0 of 312 symbols) — evidence is doc prose and shipped repos only
Instruments and the debug gauge swap the Load/Specialization colours — colour intuition from one misreads the other
The gauge's Open-in-Debugger/Export options don't work for events recorded before its report was open — open it first
Orphaned aside on model(for:options:) is a truncated Throws clause mis-rendered as a Note on three API pages
Two slightly different options values: two cache entries, two specializations, two multi-GB copies on disk
A mutable SpecializationOptions property drifting between code paths silently duplicates multi-GB cache entries
specialize() and init have no progress, stages, or cancellation contract — your Preparing UI must be indeterminate
.persistent means until the next OS update — every point release purges all specialized assets and users repay the stall
Reference pages and the caching article give opposite answers on deleting an entry a live AIModel still uses
A cache bookmark pins nothing — the entry can be deleted underneath it on OS update or storage pressure
bookmarkData is a pointer, not the model — the system deletes the entry underneath it and resolving just returns nil
deleteEntry(referencedBy:) repeats the contradictory live-AIModel deletion NOTE — release the model before deleting
ANECCompile() FAILED in the console during specialization is not necessarily an error — don't kill the run on first sight
availableKinds varies by device but not by model — a present Neural Engine says nothing about your graph's eligibility
expectFrequentReshapes on an all-static graph silently discards the AOT asset and recompiles on device
expectFrequentReshapes=true on a static graph drops AOT specialization — no log, just a slow (or jetsam-killed) load
Prewarming a host-cache graph would allocate the full static KV cache — gigabytes; prewarm the shape, not the capacity
A successful compile proves nothing about the architecture — the device is the only validator
coreai-build compile exits 0 for any requested arch — the device, not the exit code, validates the choice
AOT compiles only for Apple-Intelligence-capable devices (A17 Pro+, M1+) — older hardware isn't covered
Compile-time figures are single-author beta measurements — trust the shape (jetsam can kill compilation), not the minutes
std::bad_alloc from a Core AI load on iOS is almost always jetsam — check Console.app and the memory entitlement first
Metal Toolchain missing: model builds fail with a Metal-compiler error that doesn't point at Core AI
The number-one first-contact failure: the missing-toolchain build error blames Metal, and fresh CI runners lack it too
Throughput figures here are one community author plus one shipping app, self-declared uncontrolled — attribute accordingly
The artifact is not a function of the recipe — the exporting machine's OS changes what you ship
Same command, same weights: artifacts exported on different host OSes differ ~2x in throughput and memory on-device
coreai-build is not in Xcode-beta.app — it ships in the optional Metal Toolchain component; xcrun caches the miss
Verified absences: /documentation/updates/coreai 404s and the Updates hub carries no Core AI entries
Whole block is community-measured on beta software under uncontrolled conditions — cited because nothing else exists
Part-wide evidence weighting: zero Apple sample code — claims rest on docs, shipped repos, and attributed community work
NDArray.from_descriptor only sizes the buffer — on Linux unzeroed state reads garbage; allocate np.zeros explicitly
Inside withUnsafeMutablePointer the shape/strides are Span<Int> — not a Sequence, so no reduce; ship a product helper
memset-zeroing the whole addressable range clobbers aliased buffers — exactly the AsyncValue(unsafeBuffer:) situation
.chunked KV strategy is accepted and silently falls back to the static cache — it is not implemented
Arbitrary prompt lengths re-specialize the graph — bucket prefill into a few fixed shapes compiled once
Incident-grade community finding: the reshape hint can destroy AOT benefits — see the fixed-shape measurement below
Community-measured: expectFrequentReshapes on a fixed-shape graph kills the AOT bundle — set it only on the dynamic path
Copy-on-write copies the entire KV cache every decode step when the state buffer isn't uniquely referenced
Noema parks a placeholder in state slots during a step so the working buffer is uniquely owned — no per-token COW copy
x.mul_(2) on a forward arg silently reclassifies the input as state — positional Swift bindings shift one slot
Uninitialised state storage: nothing documents that Swift NDArray inits zero — unzeroed KV reads garbage on first use
No reset() exists — a new conversation silently continues on whatever KV the last one left in the state
Noema tracks fedTokens and prefix-checks before reuse — anything else risks decoding against another conversation's KV
Two concurrent run() calls sharing one KV cache race — exclusivity checks don't span async tasks; one loop per state set
ComputeStream(commandQueue:) does not exist on watchOS
The second async-value initializer is likewise absent on watchOS
AsyncValue's NDArray initializer is unavailable on watchOS
The AsyncValue overview's second example does not compile as written
Encode-once reuse requires caller-side caching — CoreAISegmentationEngine re-runs image_encode every call, no cache API
Grammar-constrained decoding needs logits — @Generable and forcedContinuation are unavailable on the GPU-pipelined path
'MLX 2x faster' measured a hand-rolled per-token loop — Apple's pipelined engine runs the same weights ~3.5x faster
Apple ships 21 export recipes but zero performance numbers — the community bench table is the only data, treat as such
Pipelined Core AI ties/beats MLX on dense models — but it's int8 vs 4-bit, a ship-config comparison, not iso-precision
Pipelined engine overshoots EOS into device KV — cross-turn reuse is impossible and TTFT is history/decodeRate
Whole section is one author's incident report (FB23024751, issue #5) — rigorous isolation, uncontrolled benchmarks
The ANE in-graph KV-write crash corrupts the compile cache — later loads fail ENOENT until you delete cache entries
Noema's host-cache design: KV rides as plain I/O because the ANE compiler rejects in-graph indexed KV writes
Write-mask workaround status: Mac GPU verified; iPhone GPU and ANE re-isolation still pending
Prefix-reuse section is a community fork of coreai-models — mechanism corroborated upstream, API and numbers are not
Community trimKVCache drains in-flight generation first, then clamps the processed-token counter — nothing is cleared
trimKVCache protocol default returns -1 (unsupported) so callers degrade safely to full re-prefill
Caller algorithm: track the exact fed token sequence and clamp reuse to commonPrefixLength minus one
Prefix-reuse numbers: qwen3-0.6b on an unstated Mac model and OS — treat the hardware as unverified
Models carrying recurrent extra states reject trimKVCache — hybrid/SSM architectures cannot prefix-reuse across turns
trimKVCache guards on extraStates.isEmpty — graphs with SSM/conv states return -1 and pay full re-prefill every turn
The model-selection conclusion derives from one community implementation — not an Apple claim
Known limits: the pipelined trim path is unverified (SIGTRAPs in GrowingLogitsBuffer); short chats see little gain
Intervals look fine but memcpy dominates the Time Profiler: the copy-on-write KV trap of §8.1
Numerics debugger pairs only iOS/iPadOS/macOS 27+ — no visionOS, tvOS or watchOS despite framework support
Without export-time debug metadata the Source Viewer shows no mapping to your Python — set the env vars before converting
Evidence note: zero Apple sample code — this guide rests on the shipped apple/coreai-models source read line-by-line
CoreAILanguageModel.init never calls verify() — a missing asset surfaces later as a raw Core AI error, not missingAsset
.aimodel and .aimodelc are directories, not files — file-oriented copy, zip and signing steps mishandle them
Omit image_mean/image_std and you silently get CLIP's — Qwen3-VL-class models produce degraded captions, not an error
Missing tokenizer/ falls back to a HuggingFace Hub fetch — instant on your Mac's cache, a network request on user devices
BundleKind has four cases while the repo ships six model families — the mapping is not one-to-one
The shipped SpeechModel actor needs a split bundle no exporter produces — whisper export emits one monolithic .aimodel
metadata.json's compression field records the requested compression, not what was actually applied to the weights
Bundle-format table: compression is the request (§2.11) — nothing validates it against the shipped weights
swift run defaults to Debug, where -Onone per-element closures make resets take seconds — build release for any benchmark
Commit 102f832 renamed CoreAIRunner(from:) to init(bundle:) and the metrics setters — week-old snippets no longer compile
The structure probe swallows errors and defaults to .dynamic — an ANE-meant model silently gets GPU specialization
Two models built from the same URL and settings share one engine and KV cache — the second session resets the first
Apple's own code disagrees on VLM sub-model loading (sequential vs async let) — load sequentially until resolved
autoDetectVariant calls preconditionFailure on an unrecognized bundle — it crashes rather than throwing
Inputs and states bind positionally, not by name — a graph declared in another order loads, runs, and produces garbage
Fixed bug: pipelined sampling shared one execution descriptor across steps, corrupting text at temperature > 0
VLM sampling is hard-coded to temperature 1.0 / topK 1 — the GenerationOptions temperature you pass never reaches it
.fixedSize KV allocates maxContextLength up front — multi-GB on long-context models, and every step gets slower
--kv-cache-strategy chunked is accepted but unimplemented — you silently get a fixed-size cache
Engine variant is a String?, not an enum — the Variant type is private, so typos cannot be caught at compile time
CoreAILanguageModel.init's own doc comment contradicts what the code does — a documentation trap
Same recipe and wheels export a 2.2x faster artifact on macOS 26 than on the 27 beta — quantized-Linear lowering regressed
All of §6.3-6.4 is community work: a 3-file fork commit on a pre-SAM3 snapshot, not upstream Apple code
Prefix reuse needs byte-identical re-renders — unsorted tool-call dict keys collapse the LCP and silently re-prefill
The stopTokenIds parameter is dead — values you pass are never consulted by the engines
vocabType defaults differ (.raw vs .byteLevel) — the mismatch over-constrains the grammar and generation yields nothing
Guided generation and the fastest engine are mutually exclusive — the pipelined path exposes no logits
capabilities reports guidedGeneration optimistically before the engine loads — the claim can be false until first use
HEAD renamed LanguageModelCapabilities(capabilities:) to an unlabelled init — conformances against older SDKs break
Mistral's synthetic tool-call close marker is a newline — multi-line tool-call JSON is cut at the first line break
maximumResponseTokens counts hidden thinking — a small cap can end the turn mid-<think> with no response at all
Sampling applies minP before topP before topK — not the order most stacks use, so identical settings sample differently
SamplingConfiguration.init preconditions, not throws — a topP of 0 from a config or slider crashes the app
DecodingType has exactly one case (.vanilla) — the factory and builder cannot select any custom decoding strategy
Engine selection is only via the variant string — the Variant enum is private and unvalidated at compile time
